definitions.explanation: In baseball, a complete game in which the pitcher allows no batter to reach base at all — no hits, no walks, no errors — retiring every opposing hitter in order.

examples.japanese: {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{達成|たっせい}する→達成する：22183_tasseisuru⟧。
{完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧めった⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}ない→出る：00513_deru⟧⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧だ。
examples.english: A perfect game is a record that rarely happens.

examples.japanese: {九回|きゅうかい}{二死|にし}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{打|う}たれた→打つ：01221_utsu⟧。
examples.english: It was a perfect game until two outs in the ninth, but he gave up a hit at the very end.

notes:
A baseball term for the rarest kind of dominant pitching: not a single opposing batter reaches base. Stricter than a no-hitter, which still allows walks and errors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{達成|たっせい}する→達成する：22183_tasseisuru⟧: to achieve a perfect game
- {完|かん}{全|ぜん}{試合|じあい}⟦{達成|たっせい}→達成：04816_tassei⟧⟦{投手|とうしゅ}→投手：06563_toushu⟧: the pitcher who threw the perfect game

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦ノーヒットノーラン→ノーヒットノーラン：29973_noohittonooran⟧: no-hitter — no hits allowed, but walks or errors may let runners on base
- ⟦{完封|かんぷう}→完封：06543_kanpuu⟧: shutout — allowing no runs, though base runners are permitted
